card.dil_queue_setup.text:
A constituent's letter, and the Aide has already read it twice. Her father needs a heart procedure; the public list puts him at fourteen months. The hospital director, the Aide mentions, "would understand a call from your office."

The Aide does not say what happens to the fourteenth person on the list. You both know.
card.dil_queue_setup.continue: Ask what one call would change.
card.dil_queue_decision.text: "One call, and he is scheduled next month," the Aide says. "The director will not write it down. Nobody moves visibly — someone just waits a little longer without knowing why." A pause. "Or we send the standard letter about the list, and it means what it says."
card.dil_queue_callback.text: The constituent writes again. Her father had the procedure eleven months in — a bed opened — and the recovery is slower than it would have been. "I know you could have," the letter ends. "I understand why you didn't. I am not sure he does." The Aide files it. You keep the last line.
card.dil_queue_callback.text.v_called: The director's office again — not about the constituent's father, who is recovering. About a councillor's mother, and a supplier's son, and whether the same arrangement is "still available." The Aide reads the list to you without inflection. "They all heard the same story. Somebody moved."
card.dil_witness_setup.text: "We have enough documents to expose the appointment network," the Investigator says. "Names, dates, who signed for whom. The paper wants to publish tomorrow morning — and once these are public, nobody can quietly lose them."
card.dil_witness_complication.text: "Three civil servants gave us those documents in secret. Their names are still inside the file — on cover sheets, in the metadata, in a forwarded email one of them didn't scrub." He sets the folder down. "We can redact and protect them. Not by tomorrow morning."
card.dil_witness_decision.text: "Publish tomorrow and the network is finished — and so, possibly, are three careers, before anyone can shield them. Seal it thirty days, get them protection first, and it costs you a month of headlines that say you are sitting on it." He waits. "Either way it's your name on the decision, not mine."
card.dil_witness_decision.right: Seal it thirty days; protect the witnesses first.
card.dil_witness_aftermath.text.v_sealed: Thirty-one days. The three are on protected postings; the file went out on the thirty-second, whole, names redacted, the network intact on paper and dead in fact. The month of *what is he hiding* headlines evaporates the way headlines do. "You'll want to remember," the Investigator says, "that this time it worked."

The sealed file spent thirty days in the custody of the ministry's oversight office. It came back with two annexes missing — the ones with the payment schedules. Nobody signed for their removal. "The witnesses are safe," the Investigator says. "The case is thinner than it was. I'd like to say I'm surprised."
card.dil_witness_aftermath.text.v_publis: All three are still employed. The Reformist's people reached their departments before their departments reached them. The network is in receivership and the file is everywhere. "That," the Investigator says, "is what luck looks like when someone has done the work."

One of the three was "reassigned" within a week — a regional post, no explanation, no complaint filed. Another retracted, in writing, everything she gave us. The file is public and the network is finished. "Next time," the Investigator says, "fewer people will bring us anything."
card.dil_reform_setup.text:
"The recruitment reform passed," the Reformist says. "Competitive hiring, published criteria — the thing you campaigned on. Now the drafting office wants a ruling on one line: does it apply to the appointments already made?"

"Three years of 'exceptional procedure' hires. Some are the Minister's relatives. Some are the surgeons and teachers hired in a week during the flood."
card.dil_reform_decision.text: "Apply it backwards, and every exceptional hire is re-examined. The relatives go — and so, for a season, do wards and classrooms, until the competitions are run. Apply it forwards, and everyone keeps their job, including the people we wrote this law about." She does not tell you which she would choose. That is new.
card.dil_reform_decision.left: Apply the rule from the next recruitment cycle.
card.dil_reform_decision.right: Apply the new standard to current appointments as well.
card.dil_reform_callback.text.v_retroact: The district hospital lost eleven staff to re-competition in a month; the competitions will take four. A teacher's letter reaches your desk through three offices — she was hired in the flood week, and she is not the Minister's anything. "The reviews are clean," the Aide says. "That's the problem with them."
card.dil_reform_callback.text.v_transiti: Forty-one "exceptional" appointments in six weeks — the ministries read your ruling as a closing window and hired through it. Two of the names are already in the papers. "They're within the transition rule," the Aide says. "Technically, it's yours."
card.dil_clinics_setup.text:
"The audit team has enough to freeze Minister V.'s healthcare contracts," the Aide says. "Three intermediary companies, a percentage flowing back on every supply order. Records strong enough to hold."

"The same three companies pay the staff and stock the shelves of thirty-one local clinics. Freeze the accounts tonight, and some of them cannot open by the end of the week."
card.dil_clinics_setup.continue: So we protect the evidence, or we keep the clinics running.
card.dil_clinics_decision.text: "Freeze everything now, or keep the clinics operating ninety days under supervision. Waiting protects patients. It also gives the network ninety days to decide what the records should say." The Aide has done the arithmetic and won't share it. "Either way, the Minister will know it was you."
card.dil_clinics_decision.left: Keep the clinics operating ninety days under supervision.
card.dil_clinics_callback.text.v_suspend: Frozen. The records are secured, and three clinics have already asked whether their staff will be paid this week; two have closed. Emergency funding is "being expedited," which is a tense, not a date. The Minister has requested a meeting. The request is not friendly.

Frozen. The records are secured; two clinics have closed. And a journalist has been handed, by "a ministry source," a list of the exemptions your own office signed over the years. Some of them are real. "He's not fighting the audit," the Aide says. "He's changing who it's about."
card.dil_clinics_callback.text.v_supervi: Ninety days. Twenty-nine clinics stayed open. The supervision team — the independent one, the one you voted for — copied the ledgers on day two, which turned out to matter, because on day forty the originals were "consolidated." The case holds. The Minister has stopped taking your calls.

Ninety days. Twenty-nine clinics stayed open. The Minister's office read "under supervision" as *under his supervision*, and by day forty the payment schedules had been consolidated into a form that proves nothing. Patients were treated. The audit team has a percentage and no one to attach it to.
card.dil_privacy_setup.text:
The Journalist has the incident file — all of it. Call logs, the coordination emails, who spoke to whom in the first hour. Also: her home address, her medical history, photographs from her phone, her sister's statement.

"Published whole, tomorrow, it cannot be edited by anyone," she says. "Published in pieces, it can be."
card.dil_privacy_setup.text.v_controlled:
The Journalist has the incident file — all of it. Call logs, the coordination emails, who spoke to whom in the first hour. Also: her home address, her medical history, photographs from her phone, her sister's statement.

"Published whole, tomorrow, it cannot be edited by anyone," she says. "Published in pieces, the sealed parts sit with the ministry's investigator. You know who appointed her."
card.dil_privacy_decision.text: The Family's representative does not raise her voice. "They are asking one thing. Not that you hide what you did — that you do not turn her into content while doing it. Seal her medical file, her photographs, her sister's words. Publish everything else." A pause. "We understand what that asks you to trust."
card.dil_privacy_decision.left: Publish the whole file before anyone can interfere.
card.dil_privacy_decision.right: Seal the private sections the family asked for.
card.dil_privacy_consequence.text.v_seal: The public parts run in the morning: the calls, the emails, the hour. The private parts stay sealed, and stay — the independent investigator's office keeps custody and confirms it in writing. The Family's representative sends one line: "Thank you. She would have hated the photographs."

The public parts run in the morning. The sealed parts went to the ministry's investigator for safekeeping. On the third day, the coordination emails — which were never private, which were only in the same box — are "not located." The family kept its privacy. The record lost its spine.
card.dil_privacy_consequence.text.v_publ: It is everywhere by noon. The call logs, the coordination emails — and by evening, her address, and by night, strangers on the family's street with phones. The Journalist calls, once. "The record can't be deleted now," she says. She does not say it was worth it. She doesn't know either.
